title: 2007 AMC 12A Problem 6
statement: Triangles \(ABC\) and \(ADC\) are isosceles with \(AB=BC\) and \(AD=DC.\) Point \(D\) is inside \(\triangle ABC,\) \(\angle ABC=40^\circ,\) and \(\angle ADC=140^\circ.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle BAD?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(\triangle ABC\) is isosceles, \(\angle BAC=\tfrac12(180^\circ-\angle ABC)\) \(=70^\circ.\)

Since \(\triangle ADC\) is isosceles, \(\angle DAC=\tfrac12(180^\circ-\angle ADC)\) \(=20^\circ.\)

Therefore \(\angle BAD=\angle BAC-\angle DAC\) \(=70^\circ-20^\circ\) \(=50^\circ.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: In each isosceles triangle the two base angles are equal
